subject.title: [Bug]: embedded abort settle timed out causes gateway deadlock after provider chain timeout — requires manual restart

question: After an embedded abort cannot settle, should OpenClaw force-release the retained session lock after a bounded wait, accepting takeover semantics to preserve gateway availability?
rationale: The remaining choice trades gateway liveness against ownership of a possibly resumed retained transcript write; source-level similarity alone cannot establish the acceptable session-state contract.

options.title: Require controlled reproduction before selecting policy
options.body: Reproduce the provider-chain timeout with lock diagnostics, then approve a bounded release only if takeover and late-write safety are demonstrated.

options.title: Keep graceful-only release
options.body: Preserve the current retained-write ownership rule and rely on watchdog or operator recovery until a safer liveness design is specified.

options.title: Adopt bounded forced takeover
options.body: Treat an abort that exceeds the settle bound as abandoned ownership and force-release with explicit poisoned-controller and integrity coverage.

recommendation.title: Require controlled reproduction before selecting policy
recommendation.body: Reproduce the provider-chain timeout with lock diagnostics, then approve a bounded release only if takeover and late-write safety are demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work defines the current retained-lock abort cleanup boundary most directly related to this choice.
